editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Commutative Algebra 10.85 on projective modules over local rings. Its main theorem shows every projective module over a local ring is free, relying on the previously defined projective and free module notions; the chapter does not define an additional distinct mathematical object.

Checked Stacks Algebra 10.77, Definition 10.77.1 and Lemma 10.77.2. A projective module is defined via exactness of its Hom functor, with a direct-summand characterization providing an equivalent formulation.

definitions.text: An R-module P is projective if the covariant functor Hom_R(P,−) is exact; equivalently every R-linear map P→N lifts across every surjective module map M→N.
An R-module P is projective exactly when it is isomorphic to a direct summand of a free R-module, so some Q satisfies P⊕Q≅R^{(I)} for an index set I.
definitions.context_hint: Module theory: direct-summand characterization of projectivity

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Algebra 10.62, Lemmas 10.62.2 and 10.62.6. A finite module's support is an algebraic subset of the prime spectrum, and its dimension is the Krull dimension of this support, distinct from vector-space dimension.

definitions.text: For a finitely generated R-module M, its support is Supp_R(M)={p∈Spec(R):M_p≠0}, a closed subset of Spec(R) when R is Noetherian.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: support of a finite module

definitions.text: For a finite module M over a Noetherian ring R, its dimension is the Krull dimension of Supp_R(M), the supremum of lengths of chains of prime ideals belonging to its support.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: dimension of a finite module

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Algebra 10.78, Definition 10.78.1 and Lemma 10.78.2. Finite projectivity is equivalent to finite local freeness and to being a direct summand of a finite free module; constant rank is a more restrictive additional property.

definitions.text: An R-module M is locally free if Spec(R) admits a cover by standard opens D(f_i) such that each localization M_{f_i} is free over R_{f_i}.
An R-module M is finite locally free if Spec(R) has a standard-open cover over which the localizations of M are free of finite rank, with the rank allowed to vary by open set.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: finite locally free module

definitions.text: An R-module M is finite projective exactly when it is finitely generated and projective; equivalently M is a direct summand of R^n for some finite n, or finite locally free.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Categories 4.3, Definitions 4.3.1–4.3.3 and the representable-presheaf example. This section distinguishes opposite categories, contravariant functors, and representable set-valued presheaves.

definitions.text: For a category C, the opposite category C^op has the same objects as C and a morphism X→Y in C^op for each morphism Y→X in C, with composition reversed.
A contravariant functor F:C→D is by definition an ordinary functor C^op→D; it sends each arrow X→Y in C to an arrow F(Y)→F(X).
For an object U of a category C, the represented presheaf h_U:C^op→Sets assigns to X the set Hom_C(X,U), acting on arrows by precomposition.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Schemes 26.11 and Lemmas 26.11.1–26.11.2. The Zariski topology on a scheme is locally the prime-spectrum topology on its affine open charts; affine open subschemes form a topological basis.

definitions.text: The Zariski topology of a scheme X is the topology of its underlying locally ringed space, characterized locally by requiring each affine chart Spec(R)⊆X to carry the prime-spectrum topology whose standard opens are D(f).
definitions.context_hint: Algebraic geometry: Zariski topology on a scheme
